title: Department share of payroll
statementMd:
For each department with employees, show its payroll and its share of total company payroll as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal. Employees without a department count in the company total.

Expected columns: `department`, `payroll`, `pct`.

Tables: `employees`, `departments`.

Row order does not matter.
hints: Total payroll can be a scalar subquery over all employees.
solutionMd:
```sql
SELECT d.name AS department, SUM(e.salary) AS payroll, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(e.salary) / (SELECT SUM(salary) FROM employees), 1) AS pct FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id, d.name;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
